title: Feature flags with gradual rollout and A/B assignment
description: Server-side feature flags and experiments: sticky hashed buckets, percentage rollout that only grows, kill switch, user and tenant targeting with fixed precedence, runtime config from a store with a TTL cache and change notification, audited admin changes, weighted variants with sticky assignments, once-per-unit exposure logging, anonymous-to-user stitching, a two-proportion z-test, a PostgreSQL store and a Fetch adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, TextEncoder/TextDecoder, structuredClone, crypto.randomUUID (or an injected newId) and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core usable without http.ts; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlFeatureFlagStore with your query executor; grant the app role only SELECT and INSERT on feature_flag_audit. On other databases implement FeatureFlagStore with a version-conditional flag write that appends its audit row atomically and insert-if-absent assignments, exposures and conversions.
Pass authorize(actor, action, flagKey) to allow admin operations (read, create, update, delete, audit); without it every admin call is refused.
Keep cacheTtlMs short (default 5,000 ms) and call refresh() from your pub/sub (for example Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY) to apply changes sooner; subscribe() reports changed keys.

Evaluate on the server with the session's userId, tenantId and an anonymous-id cookie; call stitch(anonymousId, userId) at sign-in and expose() only where the variant is actually rendered. Forward onExposure to analytics.
Mount createFeatureFlagHandler with authenticate(request), a trusted subject(request), and optional routes, statusFor, prefix and allowedOrigins (for cookie-authenticated admin UIs).
limitations: Buckets are FNV-1a 32 + fmix32 of "key:id" mod 10,000, the same hash as the feature-flags capability's TypeScript recipe (variants match only with an empty salt); its pre-fmix32 plain-FNV-1a versions differ.
Rollout order is fixed by the hash: the first 10% of a flag is always the same subjects, and lowering the percentage drops plain-flag subjects again.

Sticky assignments exist only after expose(); subjects evaluated but never exposed are recomputed from current weights. A new salt or a delete-and-create starts a new run: old assignment, exposure and conversion rows stay in the store but are ignored.
The z-test is a pooled normal approximation without sequential-testing or multiple-comparison correction; checking results repeatedly inflates false positives.
Change propagation between servers is bounded by cacheTtlMs unless the app calls refresh(); the in-memory store is per process and only for tests and prototypes.
The HTTP adapter has no rate limiting; evaluate with expose writes rows for the caller's own subject. Put the routes behind your gateway's limiter.

The SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs as a single connection, not on every hosted Postgres or under real multi-connection contention. Consuming-application acceptance remains a project responsibility.
decisions: precedence: kill switch > user deny > user allow > tenant deny > tenant allow > stored experiment assignment > rollout
routes: GET|POST /flags, GET|PATCH|DELETE /flags/:key, GET /flags/:key/audit, POST /evaluate; 409 conflict/exists
an exposed experiment subject keeps its variant (even at weight 0 or lower traffic); a removed variant reassigns visibly
exposures and conversions count once per unit; analysis attributes to the variant first shown (intention to treat)

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/feature-rollout.test.mjs tests/feature-rollout-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: the same flag and subject always give the same bucket, result and variant, on every instance
raising rolloutPercent only adds subjects; tenant bucketing moves whole tenants together
kill switch, user and tenant allow/deny lists follow a fixed precedence and every result reports reason, bucket and version
invalid keys, percentages, variant weights, duplicate variants and unknown fields are rejected with listed problems
flag changes reach other instances after the cache TTL without a deploy, subscribers get the changed keys, and a failing store serves the last good config
admin changes need authorize; each writes an append-only audit entry with actor, time, before and after, and concurrent writers at one version get one winner
weighted variants follow their weights, zero-weight variants are never newly assigned, and experiments are independent
exposures are recorded once per unit under concurrency; anonymous assignments survive sign-in on every device
exposed subjects keep their variants when weights, traffic or the variant list change; removed variants reassign visibly
analysis reports per-variant exposures, conversions, rates and a two-proportion z-test matching reference values
HTTP adapter: admin CRUD and audit, evaluate with expose, 401/403/404/405/409/400 statuses, trusted subject only, and overridable routes, statusFor and prefix
schema.sql applies, the audit table rejects UPDATE and DELETE, and the SQL store passes the core behaviors on PostgreSQL

changes: First release: core, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and store, and Fetch adapter.

Unreleased fix: each flag run (creation or salt change) has a runId; assignment, exposure and conversion rows are keyed by run_id so reruns start fresh and analysis ignores old runs. schema.sql changed; see its upgrade note.
